observations: Photo 0 and photo 1 show the same scene: the open back of a shipping container loaded with stacked used engines.
Engines are held on rough wooden shelf boards inside the container, many units deep and wide, too numerous to count individually.
A man in a red cap and red shirt is leaning into the container, apparently marking or inspecting engines with a marker/pen.
He is standing on the bed of a rusty flatbed truck used to transport the container.
No engine in either photo shows a readable VIN plate, part-number sticker, or casting code legible enough to match to a specific vehicle.
Engines appear disassembled from vehicles (bare short/long blocks), some with wiring and pulleys still attached, consistent with used 'tokunbo' import engines.
No oil dipstick, no compression gauge, no engine running/start-up shown, no mileage sticker visible on any unit.
A watermark reading 'G.O MERCHANTS LTD' is visible on photo 1, suggesting a bulk import/export dealer rather than a single private seller.
